COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) ADVISORY COMMITTEE

Welcome to the meeting of the Community Development Block Grant Advisory Committee. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling (818) 548-2090.
Meetings are also archived on the City website for viewing anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp.
PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon
request. Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign
language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA 91206.
If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact (818) 548-2782 during regular business hours.

  SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
  Friday, February 22, 2019, 8:00 a.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

A SPECIAL MEETING of the CDBG Advisory Committee is hereby called to meet at 8:00 a.m. on Friday,
February 22, 2019, in the City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206 to
consider the following item of business, to wit:

1.  ROLL CALL
  A. Report of Recording Secretary re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the February 22, 2019
  special meeting of the CDBG Advisory Committee was posted on or before Thursday, February 21,
  2019, at 8:00 a.m., on the Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2.  MINUTES
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the October 22, 2018, CDBG Advisory Committee Special Meeting.

3.  BUSINESS AGENDA

  A.  Reports – Information Only
  1. Receive report regarding FY 2018-19 Community Capital Improvement Project Status
  2. Receive report regarding second quarter FY 2018-19 social service performance reports and
  expenditure rates.
  3. Receive report regarding Financial Statements for community organizations.
  4. Review proposal evaluation process; and interview and deliberation protocol.

  B.  Action Items
  1.  Conduct interviews with capital improvement applicants; and deliberate and approve funding
  recommendations
  2.  Conduct interviews with social service applicants; and deliberate and approve funding
  recommendations.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items not a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes. The
  Commission may question the speaker, but there will be no debate or decision. Staff may refer the
  matter to the proper section or department for investigation and report.

5.  COMMITTEE/STAFF COMMENTS

6.  ADJOURNMENT
   Onnig Bulanikian
  Director of Community Services & Parks

  -------
  ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SERVICE
Members of the public may address the CDBG Advisory Committee regarding any item in this notice.
Service of the above Call for Special Meeting of the CDBG Advisory Committee, at the time and place
above designated, is hereby acknowledged, and the Notice required by Government Code Section
54956 is hereby waived:
Hour:  a.m./p.m., this  day of  , 20 .
By: ____________________________Title: CDBG Advisory Committee Member

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) ADVISORY COMMITTEE

  SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
  Friday, February 22, 2019, 8:00 a.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

1.  ROLL CALL
  The meeting began at 8:17 a.m.

  Present: Armenian, Avedisian, Ghazarian, Ramirez, Gharibian
  Absent: None
  Staff:  Bulanikian, Aleksanian, Kavarian, Hoonanian, Moreno Hernandez

  A.  Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the agenda for the February 22, 2019 special meeting of the
  CDBG Advisory Committee was posted on or before Thursday, February 21, 2019, at 8:00 a.m., on
  the Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2.  MINUTES
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the October 22, 2018, CDBG Advisory Committee Special Meeting.
  A motion was made to approve the minutes as submitted.

  Moved: Armenian  Second: Avedisian

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Armenian, Avedisian, Ghazarian, Ramirez, Gharibian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

3.  BUSINESS AGENDA

  A.  Reports – Information Only
  1. Receive report regarding FY 2018-19 Community Capital Improvement Project Status

  Senior Community Services Specialist Maggie Kavarian introduced the item. Armineh
  Hoonanian, administrative analyst, provided a status update on the FY 2018-19 Capital
  Improvement Projects. She reported that the majority of projects are on track and are
  anticipated to be completed by June 30, 2019.

  Committee Member Armenian had questions about the Homenetmen gym divider and
  Armenian Cultural Foundation.

  2.  Receive report regarding second quarter FY 2018-19 social service performance reports and
  expenditure rates.

  Ms. Hoonanian provided an overview of the FY 2018-19 Social Service projects, stating that all
  agencies are on track. She explained that expenditure rates are low for some agencies
  1
   because some invoices have not been processed due to the City implementing a new financial
  system or because the agency’s program year starts late.

  Committee Member Avedisian asked staff to explain what happens if agencies don’t spend all
  of their allocated funds or don’t serve who they said they were going to serve.

  3.  Receive report regarding Financial Statements for community organizations.

  Ms. Kavarian provided a PowerPoint presentation on the CDBG Ratio Calculation.

  Committee Member Armenian welcomed staff to brainstorm about how to better help potential
  new applicants, as they may need additional assistance, perhaps one-on-one counseling, as
  opposed to those agencies who have been applying and receiving funds for a while.

  Committee Member Ramirez commented that even applicants who have been applying for
  years are still not getting it right. She also mentioned that staff should tell agencies how much
  funding is available and that it is very limited.

  Chair Gharibian inquired about the amount of time that was put into calculating the ratios by
  staff.

  4.  Review proposal evaluation process; and interview and deliberation protocol.

  Ms. Kavarian provided an overview of the schedule for the rest of the meeting.

  Committee Member Ghazarian left the meeting at 8:55 a.m., but was expected to rejoin the
  meeting

B.  Action Items
  1.  Conduct interviews with capital improvement applicants; and deliberate and approve funding
  recommendations

  The following interviews were conducted:
  1. YWCA Lexington Building #1 Facility Improvements – YWCA of Glendale
  2. Glendale Community Center Facility Improvements – Catholic Charities of Los
  Angeles, Inc.
  3. YMCA of Glendale Partial Roof Repair SRO Building – YMCA of Glendale
  4. Main Campus Bleachers – Homenetmen Glendale “Ararat” Chapter
  5. Main Campus HVAC System – Homenetmen Glendale “Ararat” Chapter

  Committee Member Ghazarian rejoined the meeting at 10:48 a.m.

  Public Comment – Tara Peterson, YWCA

  After much deliberation, a motion was made to approve the following funding allocation:
  FY 19-20
  RECOMMENDED
  PROGRAM  FUNDING
  Lexington Building #1 Facility Improvements –
  1  YWCA of Glendale  $  197,450.00
  Glendale Community Center Facility Improvements -
  2  Catholic Charities of Los Angeles, Inc.  $  226,800.00
  Partial Roof Repair SRO Building -
  3  YMCA of Glendale  $  -
  2
   Main Campus Bleachers -
  4  Homenetmen Glendale Ararat Chapter  $  60,637.50
  Main Campus HVAC -
  5  Homenetmen Glendale Ararat Chapter  $  95,112.50

  Moved: Avedisian  Second: Armenian

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Armenian, Avedisian, Gharibian
  Noes:  Ghazarian, Ramirez
  Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

  Ms. Kavarian asked the Committee if it would like to provide staff with direction on how to
  distribute any additional CDBG funds allocated by HUD to the City of Glendale.

  After some discussion a motion was made directing staff to allocate any additional available
  funds up to $25,000 to the YWCA, since their recommended funding is the lowest in
  percentage of requested funds, but that if the available funds are greater than $25,000 for
  the CDBG Advisory Committee to reconvene for a meeting to decide on funding
  recommendations.

  Moved: Armenian  Second: Ramirez

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Armenian, Avedisian, Gharibian, Ramirez, Ghazarian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

2.  Conduct interviews with social service applicants; and deliberate and approve funding
  recommendations.

  The following interviews were conducted:
  1. The Zone - The Salvation Army
  2. Homeless Outreach Case Management - Ascencia
  3. Intervention/Prevention Clinical Group Counseling - Committee for Armenian Students
  in Public Schools (CASPS)
  4. Youth Employment Program - Glendale Youth Alliance
  5. Fair Housing Program - Housing Rights Center
  6. Loaves and Fishes Program - Catholic Charities of Los Angeles, Inc.
  7. Community Outreach Program - Armenian Relief Society of Western USA, Inc.
  8. GIFT Program Expansion - All For Health, Health For All
  9. We Got Skillz – Homenetmen Shant Chapter
  10. Generation Next (GenNext) – Armenian General Benevolent Union (AGBU)
  11. Intergenerational Experiences – Armenian Cultural Association, Hamazkayin
  12. Camp Y Program – YWCA of Glendale (withdrew application)
  13. Connect to Care (CTC) – Comprehensive Community Health Centers, Inc. (unable to
  attend, but still asked to be considered)
  14. Housing Support for Homeless Families – Family Promises of the Verdugos
  15. After School Program and Teen Mentoring Program – Door of Hope

  Moved: Avedisian  Second: Armenian

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Armenian, Avedisian, Gharibian, Ramirez, Ghazarian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

 The Committee discussed what direction to give staff regarding any additional CDBG funding that
 may be allocated by HUD to the City of Glendale.

 A motion was made directing staff to divide additional funding, up to $10,000, evenly among #9, 10,
 11, 13, and 14, which are Door of Hope, Homenetmen Shant Chapter, Armenian Cultural
 Association, Armenian General Benevolent Union (AGBU), and Family Promise of the Verdugos, but
 to reconvene the CDBG Advisory Committee if the available additional funding is over $10,000.

  Moved: Armenian  Second: Ramirez

  Vote as Follows:
  Ayes:  Armenian, Avedisian, Gharibian, Ramirez, Ghazarian
  Noes:  None
  4
   Absent:  None
  Abstained: None

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None

5.  COMMITTEE/STAFF COMMENTS
  Committee Member Ramirez made a comment about agencies submitting audits vs. financial
  statements, stating that she believes they should be submitting audits. She also said that agencies
  should be submitting the minutes for the board meetings during which the financial audits/statements
  are approved. She added that the employee social security numbers and names do not need to be
  included in the backup provided to the Committee.

  Committee Members thanked staff and other Committee Members.

  Ms. Kavarian announced a community meeting scheduled for March 18, 2019, during which the 2019-
  2020 Annual Action Plan would be discussed. She also announced other important dates.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 5:52 p.m.
